title: Spiritual Tourism in Andhra Pradesh: Tirupati, Srisailam and Srikalahasti
seoTitle: Spiritual Places in Andhra Pradesh: Tirupati & Srisailam | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Plan a spiritual trip in Andhra Pradesh: Tirumala and Tirupati, Srisailam, Srikalahasti, Kanaka Durga, Simhachalam, Annavaram, Ahobilam and Amaravati, with routes.
description: A guide to spiritual tourism in Andhra Pradesh: Tirumala and the temples of Tirupati, the footpaths up the hills, Srisailam's Jyotirlinga and Shakti Peetha, Srikalahasti, Kanaka Durga at Vijayawada, Simhachalam and Annavaram near Visakhapatnam, Ahobilam's Narasimha shrines, Lepakshi and the Buddhist site of Amaravati, with bookings, routes and seasons.
dek: Andhra Pradesh is home to Tirumala, one of the most visited shrines in the world, and a string of major temples from the hills to the coast.

hero.alt: The gopuram and entrance of the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, Andhra Pradesh

intro: For most pilgrims, Andhra Pradesh means Tirumala, the hill temple of Sri Venkateswara above Tirupati, run by Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD). Darshan and accommodation are booked through TTD's official system, and many pilgrims climb to the temple on one of the stepped footpaths.

The state has much more: Srisailam, both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peetha, Srikalahasti, Kanaka Durga on Indrakeeladri hill at Vijayawada, Simhachalam and Annavaram near Visakhapatnam, the nine Narasimha shrines of Ahobilam, Lepakshi's painted temple and the ancient Buddhist site of Amaravati.
quickAnswer: Andhra Pradesh's main spiritual destinations are Tirumala (Sri Venkateswara) and the temples of Tirupati, Srikalahasti, Srisailam (Mallikarjuna Jyotirlinga and Bhramaramba), Kanaka Durga at Vijayawada, Simhachalam and Annavaram near Visakhapatnam, Ahobilam and Lepakshi. Tirumala darshan and rooms are booked on the official TTD website. October to March is the best time.
takeaways: Book Tirumala darshan and rooms only on the official TTD website.
Pilgrims can walk up to Tirumala by the Alipiri or Srivari Mettu footpaths.
Srikalahasti is about 35 km from Tirupati and often combined with it.
Srisailam is both a Jyotirlinga and a Shakti Peetha.
Simhachalam and Annavaram are easy trips from Visakhapatnam.

items.name: Darshan
body: TTD offers free and paid darshan categories and some special arrangements. Book online on the official TTD website as soon as your dates are known, and carry the ID used for booking.

image.alt: The gopuram of the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple
image.caption: Tirumala

items.name: Footpaths
body: The Alipiri footpath (about 3,550 steps) and the shorter Srivari Mettu path (about 2,400 steps) lead up the hills; many pilgrims walk as part of a vow.

items.name: Around Tirupati
body: Sri Padmavathi Ammavari temple at Tiruchanur, Govindaraja Swamy temple and Kapila Theertham.

items.name: Srisailam
body: Mallikarjuna and Bhramaramba in the Nallamala forest, about 215 km from Hyderabad.

items.name: Vijayawada
body: Kanaka Durga temple on Indrakeeladri hill, and Mangalagiri nearby.

items.name: Visakhapatnam
body: Simhachalam, whose deity is covered in sandalwood paste except during the Chandanotsavam, and Annavaram's hill temple.

items.name: Lepakshi and Amaravati
body: Lepakshi's Veerabhadra temple with its famous hanging pillar, and the Buddhist site of Amaravati.

sections.heading: Stays and tips
list: TTD runs accommodation at Tirumala and Tirupati; book on the official website.
Tirupati town has many hotels for those who cannot get rooms on the hill.
Dress codes apply at Tirumala: traditional attire is expected for darshan.
Brahmotsavam at Tirumala (usually September or October) and Vaikunta Ekadashi bring very large crowds.

sections.heading: Festivals
list: Brahmotsavam at Tirumala, a nine-day festival usually in September or October, with processions of the deity on decorated vahanas.
Vaikunta Ekadashi (December or January), when pilgrims pass through the Vaikunta Dwaram at Tirumala.
Maha Shivratri at Srisailam and Srikalahasti.
Dasara at the Kanaka Durga temple in Vijayawada.
The Chandanotsavam at Simhachalam, usually around Akshaya Tritiya (April or May).
after: Festival dates follow the lunar calendar; check TTD and the temple boards for the year's schedule.

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Dress modestly and follow each temple's rules on dress, phones and photography.
Book darshan, aarti and accommodation only on official temple or government websites.
Walk the Tirumala footpaths in daylight and carry water.
packing: Comfortable shoes and socks for the footpaths

faqs.q: How do I book Tirumala darshan?
faqs.a: On the official TTD website, as early as possible; carry the ID used for booking.

faqs.q: Can I walk up to Tirumala?
faqs.a: Yes, by the Alipiri footpath (about 3,550 steps) or the shorter Srivari Mettu path.

faqs.q: How far is Srikalahasti from Tirupati?
How far is Srisailam from Hyderabad?
faqs.a: About 215 km, around five hours by road.

faqs.q: Is there a dress code at Tirumala?
faqs.a: Yes. Traditional attire is expected for darshan: dhoti or kurta-pyjama for men and saree or salwar kameez with a dupatta for women.
It is one of the five elemental Shiva temples (the Vayu, or air, linga) and is known for Rahu-Ketu rituals.

faqs.q: How far is Srisailam from Tirupati?
faqs.a: More than 300 km by road; most pilgrims reach Srisailam from Hyderabad or Kurnool instead.
The deity is covered in sandalwood paste except during the annual Chandanotsavam.
